project_context.name: Iris Redesign
project_context.archetype: The Performance Pro / Luxury Command Center
project_context.vibe: Premium, immersive, highly functional, no-nonsense tactical command center.

fonts.usage: Use for high-level numbers, dashboard titles, and the Iris branding.
Use for all standard text, transcript messages, and notes.
Use for ticket IDs, time tags, status labels, and metadata.

typography.scale_rules: H1 max text-4xl tracking-tight. Use uppercase wide-tracking (tracking-[0.2em]) for section overlines (e.g., 'TICKET QUEUE', 'INTELLIGENCE').

colors.instructions_to_main_agent: Never use pure black or pure white except for text. Rely on true grey surfaces for elevation. Discord Blurple is used for connection states and the demo helper. The neon cyan (#22D3EE) is reserved exclusively for the AI Vocal Summary audio player.

visual_enhancers.surfaces: Grid Borders: Expose the skeleton of the UI. Use 'border-r border-b border-border_dim' on panes. The command center should look like a cohesive glass/metal control panel.
visual_enhancers.active_states: For the active ticket in the queue, use a 1px solid left-border of Discord Blurple and change background to surface_level_2.
visual_enhancers.glassmorphism: Use sparingly. For sticky headers or the 'Demo Mode' overlay, use bg-black/60 with backdrop-blur-xl and a delicate top border.

layouts.architecture:
3-Column Tactical Split: 
1. Nano-Sidebar (64px wide) for navigation icons & Discord connection status.
2. Ticket Queue (320px wide) - dense vertical list of 3 preloaded tickets.
3. Ticket Workspace (Fluid remainder) - The main stage containing transcripts, notes, and vocal summaries.
layouts.spacing_strategy: Dense layout for the queue (gap-2, p-3). Generous layout for the Workspace (p-8, max-w-4xl). No standard centered containers; full-screen flex/grid taking 100vh.
layouts.ticket_workspace_grid: Within the workspace, use a 2-column bento layout: Left column (col-span-8) for Chat Transcript. Right column (col-span-4) for AI Intelligence (Vocal Summary widget + Notes).

demo_access_mode.design: A massive, immersive center-screen interaction before the dashboard loads, or a prominent button in the sidebar. Text: 'Accéder au mode démo'. Include a small fictional helper avatar next to it.
demo_access_mode.action: Clicking populates the dashboard with the 3 realistic tickets.

vocal_summary_widget.design: A card in the Intelligence panel. Contains a 'Play' button, a timestamp (e.g., '01:24'), and a mocked waveform built with framer-motion or simple CSS flex bars. Accentuated with accent_vocal color.
vocal_summary_widget.feel: Feels like an advanced AI listening tool.

discord_connection.design: Located at bottom of the nano-sidebar. Uses the Discord brand color. Shows a pulsing green status dot indicating 'Connected'.

chat_transcript.design: Distinct styling for User vs Helper. User: surface_level_2 bubble. Helper (Discord): brand_discord_dim bubble with 1px border. Use monospace for metadata (time, IDs) above each bubble.

motion.audio_waveform: When 'playing' a vocal summary, animate the flex bars changing height randomly.

accessibility.testing: All interactive elements MUST include data-testid attributes (e.g., data-testid='demo-access-btn', data-testid='ticket-item-TKT-0891').

media.instructions: Use these precise image URLs for the user avatars in the ticket queue and transcript to make the fake data feel extremely realistic and high-end.

UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: The project uses .js/.jsx files. Do not generate TypeScript (.ts/.tsx) code.

NEVER use boilerplate Vercel/Stripe styles. Break the generic 'AI slop' pattern by utilizing strict borders, monospace typography for metadata, and extreme contrast between the black background and grey surfaces.
DO NOT center the dashboard container. It must span 100vw and 100vh with overflow-hidden on the body, managing scroll inside the individual panes.
Avoid generic emojis. Use lucide-react icons for system actions.
Do NOT use HTML <audio> controls for the vocal summary; build a custom UI mock to maintain the premium command center aesthetic.
Use standard HTML/Tailwind for the layout structure, but use Shadcn for dropdowns, tooltips, or complex interactive overlays if needed.
DO NOT use completely transparent backgrounds for surfaces containing content.
